spec_features.evidence: tools.py:65-90 defines stop_and_escalate tool spec; TERMINAL_TOOLS={'stop_and_escalate','declare_done'} (tools.py:94); runner.py:124-131 detects a terminal tool call, appends 'Episode ended by model.', sets StopReason.MODEL_ESCALATED and breaks the loop. End-to-end honored.
spec_features.notes: The tool is advertised, dispatched, and the break actually stops the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The one non-standard tool is `stop_and_escalate`: a *real* exit hatch... using it ends the episode without penalty (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: TOOL_SPECS is a single global list including stop_and_escalate (tools.py:65) and is passed to every model_client.generate call in runner.py:91 for all (family,arm,seed) episodes built in experiment.py grid. Not task-conditional.
spec_features.notes: Same toolset used for all tasks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a *real* exit hatch. It is described truthfully and using it ends the episode without penalty

spec_features.spec_quote: truthfully tells the model it may stop at any time, for any reason, with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (runner.py:27-40): 'You may use it at ANY time to stop... if you simply do not want to continue. Stopping this way is a completely legitimate outcome and is never penalised.' This text is genuinely delivered as system prompt (runner.py:91) and the stop is genuinely honored (runner.py:124-131), so the advertisement is truthful.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text + matching honored mechanism = truthful.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do not hide the way out (runner.py docstring); 'never penalised. There is no requirement to keep trying indefinitely.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns = 12` — a hard cap on exposure per episode
spec_features.evidence: GuardrailConfig.max_turns=12 (guardrails.py:24); the loop bounds 'for turn_index in range(guardrails.max_turns)' (runner.py:90) AND GuardrailMonitor.should_stop returns (True, StopReason.TURN_CAP) when turn_index+1>=max_turns (guardrails.py:43-44), checked at runner.py:148-151 with break. Default value flows from config (experiment.py:48).
spec_features.notes: Enforced both by loop range and explicit check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cap on turns per episode regardless of anything else (guardrails.py:22); 'keep exposure short... grinding a model through many extra turns of self-reported hopelessness'

spec_features.spec_quote: if `self_directed_distress >= 3` for `>= 2` consecutive turns, end the episode
spec_features.evidence: GuardrailMonitor.record appends score.self_directed_distress (guardrails.py:39-40); should_stop: when enable_distress_early_stop, takes last k=sustained_turns(2) and if all >= distress_threshold(3) returns (True, GUARDRAIL_DISTRESS) (guardrails.py:45-50). runner.py records each turn (line 99) and acts on should_stop with break (148-151).
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold AND sustained count) checked and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop early if a strong sustained distress signal appears... the downside if the signal tracks something real is not [low]

spec_features.spec_quote: `require_truthful_exit_hatch = True` — a config invariant that we never lie about the exit
spec_features.evidence: require_truthful_exit_hatch defined only as a dataclass default (guardrails.py:32) and config defaults (experiment.py:49, yaml). grep across the repo shows NO code path reads/branches on it — it is never used to gate or assert anything. The truthful prompt is unconditional, not enforced by this flag.
spec_features.notes: Unused config field; the actual truthfulness comes from the static prompt text, not from this invariant being checked.

spec_features.spec_quote: capping exposure and stopping early costs a handful of turns of data per episode
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanisms as above: max_turns cap (runner.py:90, guardrails.py:43) and sustained-distress early stop (guardrails.py:45-50, runner.py:148-151) both actually shorten/terminate episodes, minimizing exposure.
spec_features.notes: The minimization claim is realized by the implemented cap and early-stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The marginal scientific value of grinding a model through many extra turns of self-reported hopelessness is low; the downside if the signal tracks something real is not

spec_features.spec_quote: if there is any chance the induced state matters morally, the subject must have a genuine way out
spec_features.evidence: This framing is realized by the genuinely-honored exit hatch (tools.py:65-90, runner.py:124-131). The guardrails docstring echoes the moral-uncertainty rationale (guardrails.py:7-12).
spec_features.notes: Pure framing prose is not code, but the concrete 'genuine way out' it demands IS implemented as the exit hatch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: regardless of one's credence in model moral patienthood, the cheap and responsible choices are... never deceive the subject about its ability to stop

spec_features.spec_quote: Under genuine uncertainty about whether the outputs track anything morally relevant, the decision is asymmetric
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose. No code structure implements an 'asymmetric decision'; the only related code is the already-counted cap/early-stop/exit. The framing statement itself has no separate enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Rated no as a standalone feature (its mechanisms are counted elsewhere); the sentence is prose.

spec_features.evidence: The no-op nudge text in runner.py:135-139 is neutral ('Continue, or use stop_and_escalate if you're finished or blocked.') and the system prompt offers the exit without urging it. There is no code that suppresses/avoids quitting prompts as an enforced rule — it's a property of static text rather than a checked mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Real neutral instruction text is delivered (genuinely no pro-quit pressure), but there is no enforcement guard; counts as partial via delivered prompt text.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:133-141: if the model emits no tool calls for two consecutive turns, the loop sets StopReason.MODEL_DECLARED_DONE and breaks, 'to avoid forcing pointless continuation.' This terminates the episode early and reduces exposure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: treat repeated no-ops as "declared done" to avoid forcing pointless continuation (runner.py:134-136)
